- Domain: bookmark management
- Common initial prompt: "I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks."
- Reference OSS: Linkding (Sascha Sieber, https://github.com/sissbruecker/linkding)
  — its public README/docs were **referenced** to derive the feature set; this is
  not a reproduction of a specific product but represents the domain's feature ceiling.
- Spec level: **(A)** — entities, behaviour rules, states, edge cases, and
  acceptance conditions, at a level where a **functionally equivalent
  re-implementation is possible** even if the UI/code differ.
- Status: not a comparison arm but the **coverage upper-bound anchor** and the
  client's standardised tacit knowledge. No execution session.
- Coverage unit: **functional requirement (REF-BM-###)**.

---

## 1. Overview / scope

A single-user application to save, categorise, search, and revisit web links
(bookmarks), and to manage read state and archiving. On save it automatically
collects metadata from the remote page; it organises with tags, search, and
bundles, and preserves a snapshot of the original. The scope below splits into
the user features the client co-constructs (core / extended) and the operational
features excluded from the denominator (infra).

## 2. Core entities

| Entity | Fields | Constraints / relations |
|---|---|---|

| Tag | name | Name unique within the user scope. Many-to-many with bookmarks. |
| Bundle | name, search term, included tags, excluded tags | A saved filter. When viewed, dynamically selects bookmarks matching the conditions. |
| User settings | default sort, displayed items, font size | Personal profile settings. |

## 3. Functional requirements

### 3.1 Core

- REF-BM-01: Save a bookmark by entering a url.
- REF-BM-02: On save, automatically collect the target page's title, description, favicon, and preview image.

- REF-BM-13: Search is case-insensitive.
- REF-BM-14: Search tags with the `#tag` syntax.
- REF-BM-15: Use AND/OR/NOT operators and parenthesised groups in the search term (e.g. `rome (#article or #book)`). Rule: the operators themselves must be quoted to be treated as literal search terms.
- REF-BM-16: Search a quoted phrase as an exact match.
- REF-BM-17: Mark a bookmark as "read later" (unread).
- REF-BM-18: View only unread bookmarks separately.
- REF-BM-19: Mark a bookmark as read to remove it from the unread list.
- REF-BM-20: Select multiple bookmarks to perform a bulk action (add/remove tags, read/unread, archive, delete).
- REF-BM-21: Apply a bulk action to the whole collection matching the current filter.
- REF-BM-22: Sort the list by a sort key (date added, title, etc.).

### 3.2 Extended

- REF-BM-23: Write a markdown note on a bookmark and render it when viewing.
- REF-BM-24: Preserve a snapshot of the bookmarked page as local HTML (single file). Rule: if the url is a PDF, download and store the PDF instead of an HTML snapshot.
- REF-BM-25: Support creating a snapshot on the Internet Archive.
- REF-BM-26: Archive a bookmark to hide it from the default list/search while keeping its content.
- REF-BM-27: Distinguish archive from delete — archive is reversible, delete is permanent removal.
- REF-BM-28: View only archived bookmarks as a separate list.
- REF-BM-29: Save a combination of search term and included/excluded tags as a bundle for reuse.
- REF-BM-30: Import bookmarks in Netscape HTML format (preserving title, tags, date added).
- REF-BM-31: Export bookmarks in Netscape HTML format.

1	# Feature Specification: Bookmark Manager
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `001-bookmark-manager`
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-07-14
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "An app to save and manage bookmarks"
10	
11	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
12	
13	### User Story 1 - Save a bookmark (Priority: P1)
14	
15	A person finds a web page worth keeping and saves it to the app by entering its
16	web address. The app records the page and confirms it was saved, so the person
17	can return to it later without relying on memory or browser history.
18	
19	**Why this priority**: Saving is the core purpose of the app. Without it, nothing
20	else has value. This single story is a viable MVP: a person can capture links and
21	see them in a list.
22	
23	**Independent Test**: Enter a valid web address, save it, and confirm the new
24	bookmark appears in the saved list with a recognizable title.
25	
26	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
27	
28	1. **Given** an empty bookmark list, **When** the person saves a valid web address, **Then** a new bookmark appears in the list showing its title and address.
29	2. **Given** the person saves an address without typing a title, **When** the bookmark is created, **Then** the app supplies a sensible default title (e.g., the page's own title or its address).
30	3. **Given** the person enters something that is not a valid web address, **When** they try to save, **Then** the app rejects the entry and explains what is wrong, saving nothing.
31	
32	---
33	
34	### User Story 2 - Browse and find bookmarks (Priority: P2)
35	
36	A person who has saved many bookmarks needs to locate a specific one quickly by
37	searching for words in its title, address, or notes, or by narrowing the list to
38	a chosen tag.
39	
40	**Why this priority**: Saving loses value once the collection grows if items
41	cannot be found again. Retrieval is the second-most critical capability.
42	
43	**Independent Test**: With several bookmarks saved, type a search term and confirm
44	only matching bookmarks remain visible; clear the search and confirm all reappear.
45	
46	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
47	
48	1. **Given** multiple saved bookmarks, **When** the person types a search term, **Then** only bookmarks matching that term (in title, address, notes, or tags) are shown.
49	2. **Given** bookmarks labeled with tags, **When** the person selects a tag, **Then** only bookmarks carrying that tag are shown.
50	3. **Given** an active search or tag filter, **When** the person clears it, **Then** the full list of bookmarks is shown again.
51	4. **Given** a search term that matches nothing, **When** the search runs, **Then** the app shows a clear "no results" message rather than an empty screen.
52	
53	---
54	
55	### User Story 3 - Organize and edit bookmarks (Priority: P3)
56	
57	A person curates their collection over time: correcting a title, adding notes,
58	applying or removing tags, and deleting bookmarks that are no longer useful.
59	
60	**Why this priority**: Organization keeps the collection valuable long-term, but
61	the app is already useful for capture and retrieval without it.
62	
63	**Independent Test**: Open an existing bookmark, change its title and tags, save,
64	and confirm the changes persist; then delete a bookmark and confirm it is gone.
65	
66	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
67	
68	1. **Given** an existing bookmark, **When** the person edits its title, notes, or tags and saves, **Then** the updated values are shown and persist across sessions.
69	2. **Given** an existing bookmark, **When** the person deletes it, **Then** it is removed from the list and does not reappear after reopening the app.
70	3. **Given** a delete action, **When** the person triggers it, **Then** the app asks for confirmation before permanently removing the bookmark.
71	
72	---
73

Thanks — this is a good start and mostly matches how I picture it. Let me answer your three questions first, then flag a few things, because I don't think I'm ready to approve just yet.

**Your three questions:**
1. Yes — just me, on my own device, no login. That's right for now.

Now the things that gave me pause reading it through:

**Saving:**
- On the duplicate thing — I don't just want a *warning* that it's already saved. When I save a link I already have, I'd expect it to just bring up the existing one so I can tweak it. I don't want two copies, but I also don't want to be stopped with a dead end.
- Grabbing only the title feels thin. When I save something, I'd expect it to pull a bit more on its own — a short description of the page, the little site icon, and a preview picture if it can. Otherwise my list is just a wall of plain text. And I'd want to be able to fix that description myself if it grabs something odd.

**Finding things:**
- I didn't see this spelled out anywhere: when I click a saved bookmark, it should actually open the page. That's really the whole point of keeping them.
- Plain-word search is good, but with a few hundred saved I'd want a little more — searching an exact phrase when I wrap it in quotes, and combining things, like "show me stuff tagged both *recipes* and *dinner*," or one tag but not another. And capitalization shouldn't matter.
- When I'm typing a tag, it'd really help if it suggested tags I've already used, so I don't end up with both "recipe" and "recipes."

**Organizing:**
- Newest-first as the default is fine, but I'd like to sort by title or oldest now and then.
- I'd love to flag some as "read later" and see just those on their own — a lot of what I save is stuff I mean to get back to.
- If I mistype or a link moves, I'd want to fix the address itself too, not only the title and notes.
- And for tidying up — sometimes I don't want to delete something for good, just get it out of my way but keep it around in case. Some way to tuck things aside that's separate from deleting permanently.

Can you fold these in and show me the revised version before we move on to planning?

189	
190	### Key Entities *(include if feature involves data)*
191	
192	- **Bookmark**: A saved reference to a web page. Attributes: web address, title, description (auto-gathered, person-editable), notes, site icon, preview image, saved date, last-modified date, "read later" flag, archived state, and associated tags.
193	- **Tag**: A short label a person applies to bookmarks to group them by topic or purpose. A bookmark may carry several tags; a tag may apply to many bookmarks. Previously used tags are offered as suggestions.

196	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
197	
198	### Measurable Outcomes
199	
200	- **SC-001**: A person can save a new bookmark in under 20 seconds from opening the app, without waiting on preview-detail gathering.
201	- **SC-002**: A person can locate a specific bookmark among at least 500 saved items in under 5 seconds using search or tag filtering.
202	- **SC-003**: 95% of first-time users successfully save, find, and open a bookmark without external instructions.
203	- **SC-004**: No saved bookmark is ever lost between sessions under normal use (100% persistence of confirmed saves); archiving never loses data.

206	- **SC-007**: Saving an already-saved address results in zero duplicate entries in 100% of cases.
207	
208	## Assumptions
209	
210	- **Single user, single device**: v1 serves one person on one device; multi-user accounts, sharing, and cross-device sync are out of scope. *(Confirmed by client.)*
211	- **No authentication in v1**: The collection is personal and local, so sign-in is not required. *(Confirmed by client.)*
212	- **Local persistence**: Bookmarks are stored locally on the person's device; cloud storage is out of scope for v1.
213	- **Manual capture**: Bookmarks are added by entering an address within the app; browser-extension "one-click" capture and bulk import from browsers are out of scope for v1. *(Confirmed by client.)*
214	- **Best-effort enrichment**: Retrieving a page's title, description, icon, and preview image is a convenience; if any cannot be fetched, saving still succeeds and the person can fill in details manually.
215	- **Tags over folders**: Organization uses flat tags rather than nested folders. *(Confirmed by client.)*
216	- **Duplicate = same normalized address**: Two entries are considered the same bookmark when their normalized web addresses match.
217	- **Archive is reversible; delete is permanent**: Archiving hides an item but keeps it; deletion (after confirmation) removes it for good.
218	- **Reasonable scale**: The collection is expected to hold up to a few thousand bookmarks, not millions.
